name: Brazil
hook: From brazilwood to Pelé: the South American giant in six facts.

facts.label: brazilwood
facts.statement: Brazil was first called Vera Cruz and was renamed for brazilwood, the tree that gave the country its name and an early export.

facts.label: the Portuguese court in Brazil
facts.statement: When the Portuguese royal family fled to Brazil in 1807, Brazil became the only South American country ruled from a European capital.

facts.label: the Amazon
facts.statement: The Amazon reaches the Atlantic at the equator near Macapá, and the Rio Madeira is one of its major tributaries.

facts.label: Rio de Janeiro
facts.statement: Rio de Janeiro was Brazil's capital and is home to Maracanã stadium; its main post office is a palace built for Portuguese rulers.

facts.label: São Paulo
facts.statement: São Paulo, founded by Jesuits in 1554, is Brazil's largest city, home to its top-ranked university and the tomb of Pedro I.

facts.label: coffee
facts.statement: Coffee became Brazil's top export by 1830; in 1932 the Olympic team sold bags of it to pay for the trip to Los Angeles.

facts.label: Pelé
facts.statement: Pelé led Brazil to the first of its five World Cup titles in 1958 and appeared in the film Victory.
